text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria posted a trade surplus of $234.7 million in the first quarter of this year after a surplus of $40.8 million end-1996, Bulgarian National Bank preliminary figures showed.
-- Foreign investment in Bulgaria amounted $307.3 million in the first six months of 1997, the Agency for Foreign Investment said. Foreign investments in Bulgaria in 1996 stood at $282.5 million.

-- Bulgaria is expected to launch a strategic programme to acquire a new credit rating and issue Eurobonds worth some $100-150 million, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Bozhkov said in an interview for national radio.
-- Bulgaria's state Biochim Bank said it expected to seal a management contract with Dutch ABN Amro Bank NV by mid-July.
-- Many Bulgarians sought medical help at the weekend as temperatures across the country topped 40 degrees.
-- Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev said he had sent an official letter to Bulgaria's chief prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev to justify police action against tax evasion.

-- Five foreign investors are interested in buying Bulgaria's ailing Dobrudzha Bank, sequestrator Snezhanka Popova said but declined to elaborate. Dobrudzha Bank has been in receivership since September 1996.
-- Bulgarian construction companies may take part in a big international project for the reconstruction of Lebanon, the Bulgarian-Arabic Trade and Industrial Chamber said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to discuss today a 20 percent one-off tax payment which would allow individuals and firms to legalise undeclared assets acquired between 1990 and end-1995 in a move to boost budget revenue.

-- Bulgaria's parliament is expected to change the heads of the national radio and television and the state BTA news agency on Thursday, said Ekaterina Mikhailova, a deputy from the ruling Union of Democratic Forces.
-- Bulgaria may face unemployment of 25 percent as a result of the restrictive currency board system which was introduced last week, former prime minister Zhan Videnov said.
